summary: Phase S1 passes boundary review after remediation commit 60397049: production imports are provider/app/transport/tenant/environment neutral, every bare production import is declared by its owning package, dependency direction remains acyclic, and all built ESM export targets load.
nonblocking_findings: S1-BOUNDARY-002 [low]: pnpm-lock.yaml was already dirty and is outside this scoped reviewer commit. Final phase integration must confirm the root frozen lock records the srs-engine Zod declaration without overwriting unrelated lockfile work.
evidence: The strengthened contract first failed exactly on packages/srs-engine/src/srs/objective-policy.ts importing undeclared zod.
After remediation commit 60397049, the focused import/boundary/build-export contract passed 10/10.

The production dependency guard uses the TypeScript AST to inspect static imports, re-exports, dynamic imports, and require calls without matching comments or template strings; scoped package names are normalized to @scope/name.
srs-engine build and check-types pass, and pnpm list shows zod as a direct production dependency.

Static scan covered 72 production TypeScript files and found no provider SDK, React, Next, Vinext, database, auth, storage, webhook, transport, process.env, import.meta.env, tenant, school, private-key, Google-key, or OpenAI-key coupling.
All production relative imports use emitted .js specifiers and the focused contract dynamically loads all 30 declared runtime exports after building.

Package direction is acyclic: knowledge-space-core depends only on zod; practice-core depends only on zod; knowledge-space-practice depends on core, practice-core, and zod; srs-engine depends on practice-core, ts-fsrs, and zod.
